strings.name: Manny Pacquiao
strings.role: Eight-division boxing champion · Philippine anti-poverty official
strings.summary: Pacquiao rose from poverty through southpaw attacks, speed and weight-class challenges to world titles in eight divisions, expanding Asian boxing's global reach. He served in the House and Senate, the latter from 2016 to 2022, and lost the 2022 presidential election. After announcing retirement in 2021, he returned to draw with Barrios in 2025. In 2026 he became secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A world boxing champion across multiple weight divisions, with influence in Asian and global professional boxing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Eight-division world champion
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won world titles from flyweight to super welterweight, an exceptional multi-division record.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained as a teenager in General Santos and earned high-school equivalency in 2007.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Sport and public service
strings.highlights.h2.text: Served in the legislature beyond boxing and joined the national anti-poverty agency in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Appointed anti-poverty chief
strings.timeline.t1.text: Sworn in as secretary and lead convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission, with cabinet rank.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Comeback draw with Barrios
strings.timeline.t2.text: Returned after his 2021 retirement; a majority draw did not win his opponent's world title.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Boxing Hall of Fame induction
strings.timeline.t3.text: Attended his formal International Boxing Hall of Fame induction.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Presidential election defeat
strings.timeline.t4.text: Lost the Philippine presidential election; his Senate term also ended that year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Senate election and remarks controversy
strings.timeline.t5.text: Entered the Senate; Nike ended its sponsorship after his derogatory remarks about same-sex couples, for which he apologised.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Lost to Mayweather
strings.timeline.t6.text: Lost the widely watched unification contest by decision.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Eighth division and House seat
strings.timeline.t7.text: Beat Margarito for a super-welterweight title and was elected to the House that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Defeated De La Hoya
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the Las Vegas fight, further expanding his international profile.
strings.timeline.t9.title: First world title
strings.timeline.t9.text: Beat Chatchai Sasakul for the WBC flyweight championship.
